Write the main text for my sales page. I'm a bookkeeper and I work only with hair and nail salons. I do monthly books, payroll for up to 10 staff, and sales tax filing.

What's true:
- I have 31 salon clients. 2 left last year, both because they sold their salons.
- I charge $199 a month. Until January it was $149, and I raised it for everyone, including existing clients.
- I close each month's books by the 10th of the next month. I missed that date 3 times last year.
- Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because the books came in clean. One said she saved $800.
- I'm one person. I don't answer the phone on Sundays or Mondays.
- The first call is free and takes 20 minutes.

Keep it to about 350 words, with a button at the end to book the call.

<final_document>
# Bookkeeping for hair and nail salons. Only salons.

You didn't open a salon to reconcile bank statements at midnight. You opened it to do great work and build a team. I take care of the books so you can get back to that.

I'm a bookkeeper, and every client I have is a hair or nail salon. I already know about booth rent and commission splits, tips running through the card machine, retail product sales, and the slow week after the holidays. You won't have to explain how a salon works.

## What you get for $199 a month

- **Monthly books.** Every account reconciled and categorized, with a clear report showing where your money went.
- **Payroll for up to 10 staff.** Paid correctly and on time, tips included.
- **Sales tax filing.** Filed for you, so it's not sitting on your to-do list.

Everyone pays the same price. When I raised my rate in January, I raised it for every client, including ones who had been with me for years. There are no introductory deals and no surprise increases for new clients.

## What you can count on

**Your books closed by the 10th.** Each month's books are done by the 10th of the following month. I'll be straight with you: I missed that date three times last year. I don't hide it, and I work hard to make sure it doesn't happen.

**Cleaner books at tax time.** Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because their books arrived clean. One owner said it saved her $800. I can't promise your accountant will do the same, but organized books take them less time.

**Someone who stays.** I work with 31 salons. Last year two clients left, and both left because they sold their salons.

## Is this a fit?

I'm one person, not a firm. When you call, you get me. I don't answer the phone on Sundays or Mondays. The rest of the week, you'll be talking to the same person who knows your numbers.

If you run a hair or nail salon with 10 or fewer staff and want your books handled by someone who understands your business, let's talk. The first call takes 20 minutes and is free.

**[ Book your free 20-minute call ]**
</final_document>

A few notes:
- **The three missed deadlines:** I wrote it as "missed that date three times." If you mean three separate client closes out of more than 350 last year, saying "3 out of 372 closes" would sound much stronger. Make sure it matches what actually happened.
- **The $800 quote:** I kept it to what you know (one client said she saved $800) and didn't suggest other owners will save the same. That keeps you clear of claims you can't back up.
- **The price increase:** I described it as fairness, meaning everyone pays the same. If you'd rather leave out the old $149 rate entirely, you can cut that paragraph down to "Everyone pays the same price."
